summary:
# NOTES: *The Crow's Inn Tragedy* (Annie Haynes, 1927; single book)

## Cast
- **Rev. James "Jim" Collyer**: rector of Wexbridge, tall, grey, kind. Luke's brother-in-law. Father of Tony. Later drained, shaken; reads note in Aubrey's blotter, burns it.
- **Luke Francis Bechcombe**: solicitor, murdered. Small, spare, grey beard, horn-rimmed specs. Firm Bechcombe & Turner (Turner retired to Streatham). Wife **Madeline**. Dislikes League of Nations; "Leicestershire" man.
- **Madeline Bechcombe**: wife. Tall, regal, aquiline, dark eyes. Blames Mrs Carnthwacke. Calls Mrs Phillimore "Sadie".
- **Anthony "Tony" Collyer**: Collyer's son. WWI, D.S.O., gassed, POW. Idle, debts. Loves Cecily. Mother = Luke's sister (Mrs Collyer, invalid).
- **Aubrey Todmarsh**: nephew (Collyer's nephew; Mrs Collyer's half-sister's son). Founder, Confraternity of St Philip, South London Settlement. Conscientious objector. Engaged to **Mrs Phillimore** ("Sadie", "the Butterfly"). Secretly **the Yellow Dog**.
- **Mrs Phillimore / Sadie**: rich American widow, fiancée of Aubrey. Actually a crook, also fortune-teller **Fédora** and Mrs Carnthwacke's maid. Boston detective identifies her. Arrested.
- **Cecily Frances Hoyle**: Luke's secretary (~1 month). Tall, thin, brown eyes, turned-up nose, wide mouth, nut-brown curly hair. Schooled at Miss Arnold Watson's, Putney. Lives Hobart Residence, Windover Square. Real father Dr James Hoyle (dead), her mother's first husband. Thompson adopted her.
- **Amos Thompson**: managing clerk, 18 yrs. Reddish-grey beard, sunken grey eyes, horn-rimmed smoked glasses, missing front teeth, stoop, thinning hair. Embezzler. Alias **John Frederick Hoyle** (artist, Rose Cottage, Burford) and **Samuel Horsingforth** (passport, Lisbon). Lives 10 Brooklyn Terrace, North Kensington (never sleeps there; library books). Arrested at Southampton on the *Atlantic*.
- **Hoyle/Thompson's "Christopher Hoyle"** signature forged over other painters' names.
- **John Steadman**: barrister/KC, Luke's cousin, Madeline's cousin. Criminologist. Keen, lazy voice, monocle/pince-nez. Disguised and captured with inspector.
- **Inspector William Furnival** ("The Ferret"), Scotland Yard CID. Foxy face, sharp grey eyes. Helped catch John Bassil.
- **Dr Hackett**: doctor, Crow's Inn, certifies strangulation, death ~12.
- **John Walls**: second-in-command clerk, florid, loyal to Luke.
- **William Spencer**: jaunty junior clerk; saw bent glove-lady on stairs.
- **Percy Johnson**: articled pupil (Rugby half-back who broke door).
- **Brunton**: 19-yr-old clerk (ex-office boy, 5 yrs); overheard Thompson in fog.
- **Hopkins**: Confraternity doorman. Short, coal-black hair, white face, fish-like silent mouth-opening, long thumb / short forefinger. Arrested at Whistone Hall (Sir Thomas Wreford). Charge dismissed at Burchester. Wife helps police.
- **Mrs Cyril B. Carnthwacke** (Bella Laymond, ex-Variety star): gambler, blackmailed by ex-lover. Brought diamonds to Luke. Strangled in car, survived; stop-press "death" announced.
- **Cyril B. Carnthwacke**: American millionaire; "guess", "Sure thing", "bless your life". "No flies on" him.
- **Mrs Wye**: Rose Cottage housekeeper. Niece helps.
- **Masterman**: detective posing as doctor on train; reports "Samuel Horsingforth, Sta. Irica, Portugal."
- **Murphy, Jackson, Gordon**: police; Gordon = carpenter.
- **Leonard Barnes**: Tony's friend, took family photo.
- **Keith & Swinnerton** (solicitors); **Arnold Wynter** (counsel) for Hopkins.
- **Mrs Collyer**: Tony's mother, invalid, Wexbridge Rectory.
- **Michael Farmore**: ex-convict, arrested at General Craven's, Mortimer Square.

## Places
- Crow's Inn Square (No. 21 corner house); Carlsford Square (Bechcombe house); Blanden Square (Carnthwackes, No. 15); Hobart Residence, Windover Square; Field of Rest (St Philip's churchyard, behind church, "just over the way").
- Settlement / Community House, South London, by river; Confraternity motto "Work and Service"; blue serge uniform.
- Brooklyn Terrace (No. 10); Notting Hill Gate; Mortimer Square.
- Burford (Royal Arms inn); Rose Cottage (black-and-white, crocuses); Burford in New Forest; Bramley Hall (Sir John Bramley); Whistone Hall (Wreford); Burchester (court/gaol); Lillinghurst (Sir John Lington); Morpeth Park.
- Burlase Street, Limehouse; 21 Burlase St "Chink-a-pin"; cul-de-sac; Golden Room (Yellow Room); house by Stepney Causeway; river Thames.
- Kensington Gardens (Physical Energy statue; Lancaster Gate).
- Southampton docks; liner *Atlantic* to Lisbon; Pentonville; Bow Street; Soho disguise shop.
- Wexbridge Rectory; Halvers farm (mortgaged); Streatham (Turner's villa); Geneva (League); Edgware Road PO; Middlesex Hospital.

## Objects
- **Collyer emerald cross**, heirloom, in secret drawer of rector's writing-table. Stones are paste; genuine emeralds later found by police. Cross exhibited at Great Exhibition 1861.
- **Glove**: long white suède, French/famous maker, left by desk. Too small for killer's hands.
- **Carnthwacke diamonds** (Russian crown-jewel necklace among them). Receipt: "Mrs. Carnthwacke has entrusted her diamonds to me for valuation and I have deposited them in my safe. Signed—Luke Francis Bechcombe." Kept by Furnival.
- **Post card** of Cecily (amateur snapshot, Field of Rest) found in Thompson's room.
- **Telegram**: "Do not mention home address. Father." Handed in Edgware Road PO 12.30, March 4th. Scraps: "Will see you as soon as possible... 5 o'clock, Physical Energy."
- **Envelope 11260** (Cecily fetches from Rose Cottage desk).
- **Time-table** with Burford underlined (L&SWR "B" pages).
- **Rubber gloves, chloroform, cord** used by killer / Yellow Gang.
- **Note in Aubrey's blotter** (woman's hand): "Mrs. C. would be at Crow's Inn with the twinklers at a quarter to twelve" (per Tony). Rector burns it.
- **Yellow dominoes, yellow masks, automatics, police whistle**, Yellow Room chairs (trap arms), knife under door with note: "The window looks straight on to the river... Jump out... from one who is grateful."
- Library book (detective novel) left at Brooklyn Terrace; Thompson's cross-stitch slippers.

## Chronology
**Ch I**: Collyer visits Luke. Tony unemployed; bear-leader post offered. Luke: "Tony can't keep himself." Cecily is Tony's girl. Aubrey "spit of" old Todmarsh. Luke will sell emeralds via appraiser. Collyer keeps cross in pocket; Luke says Yellow Gang. Luke opens cross, finds paste.

**Ch II**: Collyer visits Confraternity. Doorman Hopkins. Aubrey on Farmore's relapse; cricket, racquets. Tony arrives, mocks Hopkins. Tony and father go to pub; Mrs Phillimore in car nearby. Dinner at Luke's tonight.

**Ch III**: Luke clears appointments (Geary, Pound 11.45; Bank messenger). Tony at noon, threatens private door; knocking heard. Bank messenger waits. ~12.30 Thompson leaves with papers. Clerks break in ~2 pm. Luke dead by window, strangled. Cecily arrives; Dr Hackett pronounces murder.

**Ch IV**: Furnival & Hackett. Death ~12 noon; chloroform. Walls: Pound last client, left ~11.45. Furnival shows glove. Cecily: Luke called her ~11.45; she and Tony walked to Field of Rest; Tony arrived 20–30 min late ("couldn't find" it); back at office after 1.30; heard Luke moving. Spencer: glove-woman, yellow hair, powder, on stairs ~12.30. Collyer told by Furnival Tony was at office.

**Ch V**: Tony vs Aubrey; Carlsford Square. Steadman arrives. Tony's account (Luke wanted to see him that night). Madeline: "wicked woman." Steadman to Furnival: Thompson's disappearance; Brooklyn Terrace address found in Luke's book.

**Ch VI**: Brooklyn Terrace raid. Lodger says Thompson absent since Thursday/yesterday; Thompson paid rent Saturdays, 4+ years. Room bare (chain mattress, oil lamp, cupboard, detective novel, slippers, Cecily postcard). Library: Thompson borrowed detective fiction; description (brown beard, missing teeth, horn-rims). Steadman: room "stage-managed."

**Ch VII**: Auditors: massive fraud. Tony vs Aubrey argument; Tony implies Aubrey profits. Fingerprints: rubber gloves. Furnival: Tony opportunity but no proof. Aubrey reports Hopkins saw Thompson-like man at docks (smooth hands). Phone call: woman at Yard, "lady of the glove."

**Ch VIII**: Mrs Carnthwacke confesses glove; gambling and blackmail; diamonds to Luke; appt 12.15 (arrived ~12.30); receipt; left ~1 pm. Diamonds not in cupboard. Inspector keeps receipt.

**Ch IX**: Cecily at Bechcombe house (now Madeline's secretary). Inspector shows Cecily post card; her "favourite seat". Cecily hears door shut, chair scrape ~1.30 pm. Inference: person she heard = murderer. Cecily gives address Miss Cochrane, Morley House, Beesford. Steadman offers her a job. Telegram & letter scraps found in Cecily's wastepaper basket at Hobart. Time-table Burford. Steadman agrees to go.

**Ch X**: Burford. Landlord: Mr Hoyle of Rose Cottage, artist, sidesman; away sketching. Housekeeper Mrs Wye. Steadman notes "Christopher Hoyle" forgeries. Sir John Lington and Squire Morpeth burglaries ~1 yr ago.

**Ch XI**: Tony meets Cecily, Kensington Gardens. She breaks engagement, whispers secret ("I know"); fear of being watched. Urchin/spy present. Steadman arrives, offers Tony secretarial job for injured son of Sir John Bramley, Bramley Hall near Burford. Tony wonders about burglary there, Yellow Gang.

**Ch XII**: Carnthwacke at Yard. Fingerprint evidence: fingers too small. Carnthwacke implies Luke in debt; Steadman angry. Carnthwacke: Fédora the fortune-teller, wife told her. Furnival's notebook: "Inquire into C.B.C.'s movements."

**Ch XIII**: Tube: Tony sees Cecily with grey-haired rosy man; she's going to Burford. Inspector at station; Aubrey's engagement lunch at Madeline's. Steadman arm injured after saving Hopkins's child from Mrs Phillimore's car. Aubrey: Hopkins arrested at Whistone Hall. Tony asks about Burford; Aubrey denies knowing it.

**Ch XIV**: Luncheon. Carnthwackes arrive. Carnthwacke shows Luke photos (portrait in paper vs Frank & Burrows photo). Mrs C: "not the man." Luke "bigger", stubby beard, hair grows far back. Mrs C mentions stamped-leather **screen** before window. Mrs Phillimore: "she was keeping something back." Madeline accuses Mrs C.

**Ch XV**: Carnthwacke: murderer is someone at the house. Steadman argues. Madeline accuses Carnthwacke; Mrs Phillimore: "I don't know what to think."

**Ch XVI**: Rector & Aubrey at Community House. Police have found some emeralds (rector to identify). Hopkins story: "attempted to stop burglary." Aubrey cuts wrist; rector mops blood; finds note in blotter; burns it. Messenger: rector seems drunk, leaves.

**Ch XVII**: Rector cannot identify emeralds. Furnival & Steadman: rector hiding something. Brunton's fog story: Thompson & a woman ("shake them off"); Brunton recognized Thompson's voice, suspects Cecily. Anonymous note: "Wednesday night, 21 Burlase Street, Limehouse. Chink-a-pin." Raid planned.

**Ch XVIII**: Cecily burns Tony's letter. Mrs Bechcombe ill. Cecily to Rose Cottage; Mrs Wye. Takes envelope 11260. Tramp watching cottage (same as one Steadman tipped). Walks footpath; 6.30 train; tunnel between Rushleigh and Fairford: faint old lady, "doctor" (Masterman) and working man. Bag returned. Telegram: "Samuel Horsingforth, Sta. Irica, Portugal."

**Ch XIX**: Steadman at Luke's study; rector ill (executor). Furnival: Mrs Carnthwacke assaulted (cord round throat) in car by Victoria Gate. Cecily cries "Why should he want to hurt Mrs. Carnthwacke?" Furnival says Mrs C is secretly alive. Blanden Square: Mrs C's account. Recognized by long thumb, short index. Furnival: "Mrs. Bechcombe might tell Miss Cecily Hoyle."

**Ch XX**: Southampton. Steadman drives, disguised arm. Samuel Horsingforth arrested on *Atlantic*: alias Hoyle & Thompson. Thompson's ruse: teeth, wig, padding. Stop-press: Mrs Carnthwacke dies (fake). Thompson to Bow Street, Pentonville.

**Ch XXI**: Soho disguise shop (marmoset-faced man). Steadman transformed (eyebrows, teeth, hair). Dominoes, yellow masks. Burlase cul-de-sac; door grille; password "Chink-a-pin"; countersign "His enemies will bite the dust." Golden Room; throne-chair; trapping chairs.

**Ch XXII**: Yellow Dog's voice; laugh. Strip; bound; cords; taken to bare room by river ("low tide"). Knife under door with note (window bars move up). Steadman frees himself, then Furnival.

**Ch XXIII**: Escape through window into river; shots; Furnival hit slightly. Police launch rescue. Return to Burlase St with Murphy & Jackson. Staircase removed by Gordon; Yellow Room. Smoke/fire alarm.

**Ch XXIV**: Confraternity feast; Hopkins telegram. Aubrey arrested as Yellow Dog for Luke's murder (3 Feb) when a man in car sprang up. Long thumb/short index noticed. Cyanide attempt; inspector swapped with zinc powder. Furnival recounts Yellow Gang history: Aubrey sent down from Oxford; suspected of Collyer cross theft. Hopkins's wife rescued by Steadman's car; she housekeeper to gang. Mrs Phillimore = Boston crook. Aubrey's motive: Collyer was to stop him. Tony & Cecily reconcile; Cecily's parentage explained; ending: "The End".

## Transcriber's note (in source)
Corrected typos: "it is His Will" (V); "clerks' addresses" (V); "pieced" (IX); "few days' holiday" (XIII); "my dear" (XIII); one missing period.
